result.title: MoGloss: Joint Motion and Pseudo-Gloss Pretraining for American Sign Language Understanding
result.summary: Sign language translation and recognition have been shown to benefit from various pretraining approaches. We propose a novel two-stage pretraining approach for the motion encoder, which first learns to reconstruct masked motion, followed by joint masked prediction of pseudo-gloss units and motion. Pseudo-glosses serve as an intermediate structured representation of natural language text and are obtained from the captions by a large language model. We curate a corpus of about 1,100 hours of American Sign Language from five public datasets, estimate 2D pose for all clips and define an evaluation protocol. We then reproduce state-of-the-art translation methods and evaluate them using the same train and test splits. We propose a translation model built on our pretraining strategy, and this model outperforms the previous state-of-the-art methods Uni-Sign and SHuBERT, as well as the YouTube-ASL baseline, on the How2Sign, ASL STEM Wiki and OpenASL datasets. Furthermore, the gain from the joint pretraining using motion and pseudo-gloss grows as translation data shrinks. A classifier built on the same encoder also achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on ASL Citizen isolated sign recognition and outperforms our reproduction of Uni-Sign on WLASL2000.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出两阶段运动编码器预训练：先重建掩码运动，再联合预测由 LLM 从字幕生成的手语伪语素单元与运动，并在多个美国手语翻译与识别数据集上刷新结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 属手语翻译／识别的任务专用预训练与刷分工作，伪语素只是显式文本中间监督，未涉及 VLM 推理期 latent 状态生成、证据使用或停止决策，缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。
